sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Lehrte, a railway junction east of Hannover, has little written parking policy that we could confirm, and the city's own traffic-development page lists its topics without saying anything about parking [4]. We found no readable official source on current on-street fees, resident parking or parking-disc zones. The one rule we found is a parking-disc rule from March 2017 at the Zuckerzentrum car park, reintroduced after complaints that long-term parkers blocked customer spaces, allowing three hours Monday to Saturday from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m.; its current status was not checked [13]. In May 2026 the city announced plans for bicycle streets in the core town and a comprehensive parking survey in the quarter between Bahnhofstraße, Südring, Westring and Berliner Allee, scheduled for early June 2026, and we did not find its results [17]. On 1 July 2026 the council adopted a master plan for Bahnhofstraße and the town-hall quarter, after a design competition covering about 4.4 hectares south of the station [3]. The master plan was described in September 2025, before adoption, as envisaging a new station building with a travel centre and a central quarter garage, which the adopted plan's page does not confirm [15]. In August 2026 the administration proposed to dedicate the park-and-ride site at Sternstraße in Hämelerwald as a public parking space under the state road act, because cars without number plates were being left there and the waste company does not clear undedicated land [10].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The park-and-ride lots are being extended. In November 2024 the Region Hannover committee approved extending the park-and-ride at Ahlten station from 55 to 116 spaces in a first phase, with 28 more possible later; construction was planned for autumn 2026, and that is a plan as of the article [12]. At Hämelerwald the Region and the town opened 117 additional spaces on the south side of the station on 1 February 2017, at a cost of about 716,000 euros, of which the state paid 445,000 [11]. A 2014 development plan for a multi-storey car park in the town centre described six levels with 355 spaces, 233 of them park-and-ride, and is not a current inventory [2]. On charging, the municipal Lehrter Parkhausgesellschaft took over the public charging network from the Stadtwerke on 1 January 2026 and operates 23 locations, mostly with two 22 kW points per post, with new sites in 2026 at the LSV sports park and the Amtsgericht [8][9].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The numbers for the station car parks do not agree. Deutsche Bahn lists the covered Poststraße car park with 354 spaces, paid, at 1.00 euro for two hours and 12.00 euros for 24 hours [0]. The Region Hannover's portal lists the Lehrte park-and-ride on Bahnhofstraße as free with 305 car spaces and 518 bike spaces, which may not be the same facility, and Ahlten with 54 car spaces and Immensen-Arpke with 91 [7]. For Hämelerwald, DB lists three lots with 52, 113 and 84 spaces, while the Region's portal lists the Sternstraße site as free with 157 spaces, including 2 for reduced mobility and 2 with e-charging, and 202 bike spaces [1][6]. The town-owned Parkhausgesellschaft is the company behind the garage and the charging network [8].

Our data cover the Hämelerwald park-and-ride, whose feed gives 157 spaces, matching the Region's portal, for about 27 days since late September 2026. Occupancy averaged about 15% on both weekdays and weekends, with a peak of 31%, so the lot is rarely busy. The Lehrte station car parks are not in our data.
